section_summary: This section documents the work and reception of the Shoup Taxation Mission, headed by Dr. Carl S. Shoup, which conducted an intensive study of the Japanese tax system and proposed sweeping structural and administrative reforms. The despatches and enclosed press reports and releases detail recommendations for reducing personal income taxes, introducing a net worth tax, revising corporate and real estate levies, revaluing business assets, and granting broader fiscal autonomy to local governments. Also included are an internal State Department memorandum summarizing the mission's findings and a consular report illustrating the severe tax, labor, and financial pressures confronting Japanese small businesses under Occupation stabilization policies.

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting and reporting on the Shoup Taxation Mission's recommendations for reforming the Japanese tax system, including press releases and press commentary.
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch transmitting a summary press release and Japanese press reactions regarding the recommendations of the Shoup Taxation Mission led by Dr. Carl S. Shoup. The mission proposed comprehensive revisions of Japanese national and local tax structures, including personal income tax reductions, a net worth tax, corporate asset revaluations, and increased fiscal autonomy for local governments. Japanese political and financial leaders generally welcomed the proposals as fostering economic recovery and capital accumulation, though some concerns were raised regarding the burden on lower-income groups.
subfiles.title: Recommendations of Shoup Taxation Mission

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting the full report and appendix of the Shoup Taxation Mission and summarizing its contents and Japanese public and editorial reactions.
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch reporting the official release of the Shoup Mission's comprehensive report and appendix on Japanese taxation, including transmittal correspondence between General MacArthur and Prime Minister Yoshida. It outlines the report's fourteen chapters, emphasizing the need for an equitable, modern tax system to replace arbitrary practices and counter communist propaganda. The despatch also reviews detailed Japanese press reactions regarding corporate asset revaluations, local tax autonomy, and the burden on wage earners.
subfiles.title: Issuance of Report on Japanese Taxation by the Shoup Mission
